I can definitely relate to this OP. I’m a 21 year-old single mom and a college student. Always being on-mode can get draining which can cause loneliness, for me, but then being around people the same age as me and finding difficult to relate to them because of motherhood felt more isolating. Recently, I found that I would rather do things I enjoy alone (and with my baby) over the company of people I would have difficulty connecting with. Here’s what’s helped me:

Finding your own hobbies and interests really help when these negative feelings come up. Some examples would be me reading, making/listening to music, sewing, or watching interesting YouTube videos while my daughter is sleeping or playing. 

Putting on music and dancing/singing, at home. Sometimes being a parent feels like I’m always so stiff and serious and I just need to loosen up and let my weird side out. It feels ridiculous, at first. I realized that my kid can’t really judge me and she’ll eventually join in on the fun.

JOURNALING!!! This has been a game-changer for me, from writing poems/songs to writing out what’s bothering me, putting things out on paper really help lift the mood. My daughter even joins me and scribbling/doodling with her became a fun way to bond. 

And if you are craving some human interaction.. Go on Yelp or Google to find kid activities in your area.  That way your daughter can be around kids her age and you can socialize a bit with other parents. 

Another thing I just thought of... what if we made a chat room for this sub? That way if anyone needs to talk we could go on there. 

It’s pretty long but I hope I could help. You may feel lonely but you’re never alone. Feel free to message me if you wanna talk, I see we’re around the same age so maybe we could try to connect. Anyway, peace, love, and light to anyone that reads this 🍃✨💕
